passage:
The bell at Green Street Library broke on Monday. Usually, it rang when someone opened the door. Without it, the librarian, Mr. Huang, did not always notice visitors.
At first, he wanted to fix it quickly. But then he found something interesting. Without the bell, people entered more quietly. They looked around before asking questions. Some visitors even helped others find books.
The library felt calmer.
When the repair worker came on Friday, Mr. Huang asked him to make the bell softer instead of louder.
The old bell had done its job, but it had also made every entrance feel sudden. The new sound was gentle. It reminded Mr. Huang that not every problem needs to be fixed in the same way it was before.
